response.answer: Spousal benefits under Social Security allow a spouse (even if they never worked) to receive benefits based on the worker's record, generally if the spouse is at least 62 and the worker is receiving retirement or disability benefits. Divorced spouses may qualify if the marriage lasted at least 10 years, they are 62 or older, unmarried, and not entitled to an equal or higher benefit on their own record. A pension from non-Social-Security-covered work may reduce spousal benefits.
